summary: Udenafil is a selective phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) inhibitor used to treat erectile dysfunction and, in some regions, lower urinary tract symptoms associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia. By inhibiting PDE5 it increases cyclic GMP in vascular smooth muscle, enhancing nitric-oxide-mediated relaxation and penile blood flow during sexual stimulation. It is relatively long-acting. It is not FDA-approved (marketed mainly in South Korea and some other countries as Zydena); this record is based on regional/manufacturer labeling. Co-administration with nitrates is contraindicated because of the risk of severe hypotension.
indications: Treatment of erectile dysfunction in adult men
Lower urinary tract symptoms associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia (region-specific approval)

dosage.d: 100 mg approximately 30 minutes before sexual activity; may adjust between 100 and 200 mg based on response and tolerability
dosage.n: Maximum one dose per day; effect requires sexual stimulation
Allows readiness without timing to activity; individualize

dosage.d: Use a lower starting dose and titrate cautiously
dosage.n: Avoid in severe impairment unless benefit outweighs risk

admin: Administer orally, with or without food
For on-demand use, take about 30 minutes before sexual activity
Do not exceed one dose in 24 hours
Confirm the patient is not taking nitrates or nitric oxide donors before prescribing
Counsel that sexual stimulation is required for effect
moa: Udenafil selectively inhibits phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5), the enzyme that degrades cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) in the corpus cavernosum. During sexual stimulation, nitric oxide release increases cGMP; by blocking its breakdown, udenafil sustains smooth muscle relaxation and increased blood flow into the penis, producing an erection. PDE5 inhibition also relaxes smooth muscle in the prostate and bladder, relevant to BPH symptoms.

absolute: Concurrent use of organic nitrates or nitric oxide donors (risk of severe hypotension)
Concurrent use of guanylate cyclase stimulators (e.g., riociguat)
relative: Severe cardiovascular disease where sexual activity is inadvisable
Recent stroke or myocardial infarction; unstable angina; significant hypotension
Hereditary degenerative retinal disorders (e.g., retinitis pigmentosa)
Anatomical penile deformity or conditions predisposing to priapism (sickle cell, myeloma, leukemia)

preg: Udenafil is not indicated for use in women, including during pregnancy.
lact: Udenafil is not indicated for use in women, including during breastfeeding.
renal: Use with caution; reduce the dose and titrate carefully in moderate impairment and avoid in severe renal impairment unless the benefit outweighs the risk.
hepatic: Use with caution; reduce the dose in hepatic impairment as clearance may be reduced, and avoid in severe impairment.

major: Organic nitrates / nitric oxide donors - severe hypotension; contraindicated
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, ritonavir, clarithromycin) - markedly increased udenafil levels; reduce dose
moderate: Alpha-blockers - additive blood pressure lowering; start low and separate dosing
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excessive alcohol - additive vasodilation, hypotension, and dizziness.
interactions.diagnostics: No significant laboratory test interference reported.

serious: Sudden vision loss (non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy)
rare: Cardiovascular events during sexual activity in at-risk patients
emergency: Sudden loss of vision or hearing
Chest pain or fainting after dosing

monitoring: Blood pressure, particularly in patients on antihypertensives or alpha-blockers
Cardiovascular fitness for sexual activity before prescribing
Erectile response and any prolonged erection
counsel: Take about 30 minutes before sexual activity (on-demand) or once daily as prescribed; the medicine works only with sexual stimulation
Never use with nitrate heart medicines (e.g., nitroglycerin) - the combination can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure
Seek emergency care for an erection lasting more than 4 hours, or sudden vision or hearing loss
Limit alcohol, which can increase dizziness and lower blood pressure
Stop and get help for chest pain or fainting during or after sex
Tell your doctor about all medicines, especially for blood pressure or prostate
pk: Erectile effect within about 30 to 60 minutes
Peak plasma concentration about 1 to 1.5 hours after dosing
Effect can persist for up to about 24 hours or longer
Store per product labeling at controlled room temperature, protected from moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved; marketed mainly in South Korea (Zydena) and some other countries - this record reflects regional/manufacturer labeling
Relatively long half-life supports both on-demand and once-daily dosing
Absolutely contraindicated with nitrates and guanylate cyclase stimulators (riociguat)
Reduce dose with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and with alpha-blockers/antihypertensives
Priapism and sudden vision/hearing loss are class warnings requiring urgent care
missed: For on-demand use there is no scheduled dose to miss - take only when needed before sexual activity and not more than once daily. For once-daily dosing, take the missed dose when remembered unless it is near the next dose, then skip it; do not double up.
overdose: Overdose may intensify dose-related adverse effects such as headache, flushing, dizziness, and hypotension. Management is supportive, including positioning and fluids for hypotension; dialysis is unlikely to be helpful given high protein binding. There is no specific antidote. Seek emergency care for priapism or severe cardiovascular symptoms and contact a poison control center.
